summary: Set up a cron-driven pull-sync on node2 that fetches /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) every 5 minutes via passwordless SSH (cluster keypair) and applies it only when changed. Verified two independent live updates on node1 propagated to node2 automatically within a cron cycle, and confirmed the mechanism survives a reboot of both nodes (new boot IDs observed, cron/ssh services and synced data all recovered).
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2: /etc/inventory/app.conf did not yet exist on either node; RHEL7.9 on both; sshd/crond active; no rsync installed
Installed the cluster SSH keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node2, CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY appended to authorized_keys on both nodes) to enable passwordless node2->node1 SSH
Created source-of-truth /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 (root-owned dir, sudo required)

Wrote /usr/local/bin/sync-inventory-conf.sh on node2: pulls app.conf from node1 over SSH (sudo -n cat), compares checksums, and only overwrites the local copy on change; logs to /var/log/inventory-sync.log
Installed a crontab entry on node2 running the sync script every 5 minutes (well under the 15-minute requirement)
Manually validated the script, then edited app.conf on node1 twice and confirmed cron auto-synced node2 both times with matching sha256 checksums

Captured pre-restart boot_id/service/data baseline on both nodes, restarted node1 then node2 one at a time via shutdown -r now, polled until SSH returned, and confirmed boot_id changed on each and services/cron/data recovered
Performed a final post-reboot end-to-end sync test (new content on node1) and confirmed automatic cron-driven propagation to node2 with matching checksum

evidence.requirement: node1 app.conf exists and is treated as source of truth
evidence.summary: Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 with initial content and captured its sha256sum.

evidence.requirement: Passwordless SSH established for sync mechanism
evidence.summary: Deployed cluster SSH keypair on both nodes and confirmed node2 can SSH to node1 as antrieb with sudo -n access to app.conf.

evidence.requirement: Sync script created and functioning on node2
evidence.summary: Wrote /usr/local/bin/sync-inventory-conf.sh and ran it manually; node2 copy matched node1 sha256 d39ed023f41411f25e15dfb583845355e38b803eebe087cfe4941cb177f2512a.
Installed crontab entry on node2 running the sync script every 5 minutes.

evidence.requirement: Change on node1 propagates to node2 automatically (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Modified app.conf on node1 (sha256 ca64030e...); cron log on node2 showed an automatic sync at 10:40:01 and node2's file matched node1's checksum exactly.
Captured node1 boot_id 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6, sshd active, and app.conf checksum before restart.
Captured node2 boot_id 95e2f83d-06d0-47d9-8151-0f56c34060f1, crond/sshd active, cron entry present, and app.conf checksum before restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Issued shutdown -r now on node1 (ack returned before disconnect), observed connection timeouts while down, then reconnected with new boot_id 2c436ff6-2694-4c6a-8ad6-af86cd0ea3ee, proving a real reboot occurred.
sshd active again and app.conf content/checksum unchanged (ca64030e...) after node1 reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Issued shutdown -r now on node2 (ack returned before disconnect), observed connection timeouts while down, then reconnected with new boot_id 1f00229c-d867-4053-a0c2-18c544fb4a9e, proving a real reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of services, cron config, and data
evidence.summary: crond/sshd active again, crontab sync entry intact, and app.conf checksum matched node1's (ca64030e...) after node2 reboot.

evidence.requirement: Sync mechanism still functions automatically after both restarts
evidence.summary: Appended new content to app.conf on node1 (sha256 6c9387db...) post-reboot; cron log on node2 recorded an automatic sync at 17:55:01 and node2's file checksum matched node1's exactly, confirming the 15-minute sync requirement holds after both node restarts.
